description: What ModelBlaster can GENERATE CODE FOR, as opposed to what the hardware can execute. `cores/spacemit_k1.json` is the hardware capability registry: which ops a core can run, and that IME traps on cluster 1. This file is the compiler's half of the same interface, and the two are not interchangeable -- a schedule can be perfectly executable and still impossible to generate. Every rule here was learned by a build failing, and each carries where it is enforced so the two sides cannot drift.
why_this_file_exists: The scheduler's option space was wider than the compiler's. XPU-RT's `shard` machine-combination mode lets every periodic INSTANCE of a dispatch pick its own aligned core block, which for a convolution is not buildable -- the packed weight array is materialised per shard while generating the skeleton, so the width must be one value per dispatch. Nothing told the scheduler that, so it produced valid schedules the compiler refused: on the 5-net ladder rung greedy gave `dronet` dispatches 0, 3, 8 and 9 two or three different widths across their five instances, and the board build died at stage 1 of 5 -- after extracting and generating for every model -- with an error raised from inside a shell script. A contract turns that into a solver constraint, or failing that into a check that costs milliseconds and names the dispatch.

uniform_width_across_instances.statement: Every periodic instance of one dispatch must be given the same core width.
uniform_width_across_instances.why: The packed weight array is emitted per shard at skeleton-generation time, so one generated model cannot carry two layouts for one dispatch. The K3 simple-layer pool ops (k3-work TASK-017) carry no packed weights, but schedule_shards takes one width per dispatch for every dispatch it is given, so they are pinned too.

width_divides_output_channels.statement: The core width must divide the op's OC exactly when the op is split by output channels. A conv2d_s8 split by output rows (conv_split_axis) is exempt.
width_divides_output_channels.why: Each shard receives its own OC slice of the packed weights; a remainder has nowhere to go.

conv_split_axis.statement: On a K3 backend (name starting with one of backend_prefixes; XPU-RT reads the same prefix in module_name), a conv2d_s8 given width w > 1 is split by output rows when OH >= w and OH*OW >= min_pixels, else by output channels (which then needs w | OC). The fused conv ops, and every other backend, keep the output-channel split.
conv_split_axis.why: Measured on the K3 (k3-work TASK-016 step 3): the channel split repeats the kernels' input-side setup on every core and, on the A100's 1024-bit vectors, leaves the RVV kernel's OC-wide lanes idle; the row split shares neither problem and scaled 1.7-4.1x at width 8 against 0.7-1.9x. It loses where a layer has too few output pixels for the width; min_pixels = 36 kept every K3 backend within 10% of the per-layer best.
conv_split_axis.checkable_from: schedule (OH, OW and OC are in module_name)

runtime_sliceable_ops.statement: These may take a different width in every instance, and need no codegen annotation.
runtime_sliceable_ops.why: Row-major weights are sliced at runtime using the entry's own pool width, so nothing is baked at generation time. Recorded explicitly because the width check was once applied to every dispatch, which refused schedules that generate perfectly well -- `ffn_block` has no convolution at all and was still rejected for varying a linear's width.

linear_split_axis.statement: A linear is split on M. An N-axis split is refused when M > 1.
linear_split_axis.why: The N-split emits one output tile per shard and aliases them into a single output buffer at offset off_m*N; with M > 1 the rows interleave and the tiles overlap. M-split is offset off_m*K on the input and shares weights and bias.

ime.statement: IME kernels exist for int8 linear, matmul and (since 2026-09-01) convolution, and only on cluster 0.
ime.why: smt.vmadot executes on harts 0-3 and TRAPS on 4-7, established by a per-core SIGILL probe -- so this is a correctness constraint, not a performance hint. There is no fp16 matrix hardware; fp16 reaches IME only through an accuracy-gated int8 requant.
ime.selection_policy: per dispatch, only where MEASURED faster than RVV (pipeline/ime_cost.py). The win tracks K=IC*KH*KW and N=OC (tile fill), not M.

machine_combinations.statement: A combination contains cores of one kind, as an aligned block.
machine_combinations.why: `kind` is how the runtime resolves an abstract CPU_P#n slot to a hart -- it takes the n-th core of that kind -- so a cross-kind combination is attributed to one kind's backend. Alignment is what makes overlap tests honest.

staged_ir_networks.statement: These networks cannot be extracted by name and must be supplied as a built IR directory containing graph.json, weights.npz and io.npz.

yolov8_nano_64x96.build: MODELBLASTER_YOLOV8N_INPUT=64x96 MODELBLASTER_YOLOV8N_NC=2 MODELBLASTER_YOLOV8N_WEIGHTS=<repo>/sims/models/warehouse/yolov8n_gate_person_64x96.pt python -m pipeline.extract_graph --model yolov8_nano --quant int8 --out-dir <dir>
yolov8_nano_64x96.why: The name registers the yolov8_nano module built at a different input size AND a different class count, so `extract_graph --model yolov8_nano_64x96` has nothing to extract. The DEPLOYED detector is a 2-class (gate, person) fine-tune: the profile database records dispatch 89 as conv2d_s8 with OC=2 and the detect cat as C_inputs64|2xC_total66, and the checkpoint's cv3.*.2.weight is (2,64,1,1).
yolov8_nano_64x96.weights: sims/models/warehouse/yolov8n_gate_person_64x96.pt (in the ORIGINAL XPU-RT checkout, not this one)
yolov8_nano_64x96.do_not_omit_the_weights: A default extraction gives the stock COCO-80 head. It does not fail -- it produces a DIFFERENT NETWORK under the same name with the same 98 dispatches, and a board run against it measures 10 dispatches (2.02% of yolo time: the three final cls convs and the cats) doing more work than the schedule assumed. MODELBLASTER_YOLOV8N_NC=2 against the stock weights is refused, which is the only reason this was caught.

shareable_ops.statement: Only these ops can be spread over several cores; every other op runs on the first core of a multi-core group while the rest wait. An op listed under backend_prefixes is shareable only on a backend whose name starts with one of its prefixes (XPU-RT reads the backend in module_name). A scheduler must not offer any other op, or any op on another backend, more than one core.
shareable_ops.why: An op spreads only if ModelBlaster has a pool path for it (a parallel_<op> wrapper in pipeline/generate_skeleton.py, or an mbp_<op> wrapper from pipeline/k3_pool_ops.py on the K3 backends, k3-work TASK-017). A multi-core profile of any other op measures the same single-core code, so a 'faster' wider width there is noise, not a gain (k3-work TASK-016).
shareable_ops.derived_from: pipeline/generate_skeleton.py::shareable_ops and ::shareable_op_backends (pipeline/tests/test_conv_row_split.py keeps this rule equal to them)
